name: Factbase (Roll Call; formerly Factba.se)
what: Searchable archive of Trump, Biden and Harris public statements: transcripts, video, Trump tweets. No Elon Musk coverage found.
why_it_matters: The closest existing per-person 'everything said' archive with transcript-plus-video. Beats a blank Musk search only if we need a political baseline. Does not cover Musk, so it cannot replace our X/YouTube build.
numbers: 2017 reporting: over 2.6M words and 30,000+ tweets, interviews back to 1987 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factba.se citing 2017 press). Later snapshot cited 4.7M words (same Wikipedia-linked reporting, year not pinned). Founded Jan 2017; FiscalNote acquired parent FactSquared Jan 2021.
ui_notes: Search box plus filters (Event Type, Media, People: Biden, Harris, Trump; 'Donald Trump Tweets' section); sort Oldest/Newest. Transcripts carry sentiment and keyword tags; text linked to video moments. Filters loaded as 'Loading...' on our fetch, so filter behaviour is partly unverified.
note: Senate Dems page says in late May 2025 the White House quietly stopped posting official transcripts; Factbase updates periodically. Deleted-post handling not stated anywhere we read.

name: Trump Twitter Archive
what: Searchable archive of @realDonaldTrump tweets, including deleted ones captured from Sept 2016.
why_it_matters: Best-known single-person tweet archive with deletion capture. Good template for the tweet-level record (date, device, deleted flag) that we need for Elon.
numbers: About 56,000 tweets from 2009 (secondary report, qz.com era, unverified current count). Deleted-tweet capture from Sept 2016 (same secondary source).
ui_notes: Search and filter by date and posting device (per secondary reporting). Our fetch returned only the title, so layout is unverified.
note: Current site status unconfirmed; the site returned only a title on fetch. Check the Wayback snapshot before relying on it.

name: bpb27/trump_tweet_data_archive
what: Machine-readable JSON archive of Trump tweets, zipped by year, refreshed hourly.
why_it_matters: A bulk-downloadable schema we can copy: id_str, created_at, source (device), text, favorite and retweet counts. Gives us a field list for Elon rows.
numbers: Files cover 2009 to 2018 by filename (master_2009.json.zip to condensed_2018.json.zip). Repo shows 10,191 commits (not tweets). Tweet count not stated on page.
ui_notes: No UI. Data-only. Condensed vs master files; master holds full API response.
note: No deleted-tweet flag seen in the sample record. Last-commit date and license not shown on the page. | check: GitHub commits API: last page 10,191 commits (matches row); repo 203 stars, 25 forks.

name: Politwoops (ProPublica, ex-Sunlight Foundation)
what: Archive of deleted tweets by politicians. Frozen; no longer updated after X disabled the deletion-tracking feature.
why_it_matters: The only large-scale deleted-post archive for public figures. Shows the deletion-tracking method (poll, record time to delete) that we would need to adopt for Elon deletes.
numbers: About 1.1M deleted tweets by 10,404 politicians in 35 countries (Open State figure, via search summary; source has a typo flagged). ProPublica collected roughly 1M deletions 2012 to 2023 (secondary search summary).
ui_notes: Browse by politician name or party; each deletion shows what was deleted and when. Records time between post and deletion. No search API or bulk download per summary.
note: Our fetch of the ProPublica page returned a partial 2025 snapshot 'for archival purposes'. Internet Archive mirror item (archive.org/details/politwoops) returned 404 with Retry-After 3600. | check: projects.propublica.org/politwoops: no count of deleted tweets, politicians or countries on the page; archive last updated 2022 and no longer maintained, so the 1.1M figure is unsupported by the cited source.

name: Internet Archive TV News Search
what: Search of closed-caption text across US TV news broadcasts, with clips you can borrow and watch.
why_it_matters: Spoken-word TV record for Musk appearances on news channels, with station and time. Captions are real-time and error-prone, so 'Musk' may be misspelled in the index.
numbers: Launch 2012: 350,000 broadcasts (blog.archive.org). A later, less-established site claims 4,430,000 broadcasts from mid-2009 (unverified).
ui_notes: Search by caption phrase; filter by network, show and time window; short streaming clip per hit. Our fetch returned only the title, so result layout is unverified.
note: Caption-based, so a quote here is a transcript line with a station and time, not a verified text of what was said. | check: archive.org advancedsearch collection:tvnews numFound 4,580,741 today; row's 4,430,000 (from a secondary site) is within 10%; the 350,000 at 2012 launch was not checked.

name: Wikiquote: Elon Musk
what: Community quote page grouped by year, with venue, date and link to tweets, interviews, books and speeches.
why_it_matters: The best free per-year citation pattern for Musk on a public page. Already in the blind map as Wikiquote basics; this row adds the citation format it uses.
numbers: About 200 quotes in the visible main section, plus a few in 'Quotes about Musk' (page truncated at 100k chars of 107,633). The 2007 section alone has about 40 quotes from archived pages on evancarmichael.com (fetched page).
ui_notes: Quotes under year headings; each entry names venue (interview, podcast, book, speech, article, tweet) and a date (day-month-year, or year only). Citations link to the source or an archived copy, or cite a news report. Notes flag later deletions. Example: tweet dated 19 Nov 2017 with link; Axios interview 25 Nov 2018 (season 1, episode 4).
note: Many entries cite secondary news rather than the original, and some tweets have no link ('Post on X'). Not exhaustive; we cannot tell which entries are complete.

name: Quote Investigator (Musk-tagged pages)
what: Attribution research articles on quotes credited to Musk, with dated write-ups and a verdict on origin.
why_it_matters: Shows the verification standard we want on a quote record: earliest known source, dated, with apocryphal flags. Three Musk pages listed.
numbers: 3 Musk-tagged articles on the tag page: 2017-09-24 (updated 2025-04-14) on 'mud ball' extinction line; 2019-08-29 (updated 2025-04-04) on simulation; 2023-11-19 (updated 2024-01-20) on small fortune. Verdicts not visible in tag excerpts.
ui_notes: Each article: title, date, updated date, 'Apocryphal?' questions, then origin with earliest known citations. Tag page lists title and date only.
note: Coverage of Musk is thin (3 pages). Use as a method, not a source of Musk quotes.

name: Snopes fact-check: Musk education vs intelligence quote
what: Fact-check of a viral Musk quote: searched for any tweet or statement, found none, traced earlier similar wording.
why_it_matters: Shows how a missing quote is handled: 'no record found' plus earliest similar wording (a 1977 newspaper column). Our record needs a 'not found' status, not silence.
numbers: No record of the quote in Musk's tweets or statements (per search summary of Snopes). 1977 newspaper column as earliest similar wording.
ui_notes: Article text with verdict; no per-quote archive view.
note: Read only via search snippet, not full fetch.

name: Birdwatch Archive
what: Archive of X Birdwatch community notes, each linked to the post it annotates by ID.
why_it_matters: Keeps fact-check notes on posts, which can outlive deleted posts. A possible side source for Musk posts that were later edited or removed.
numbers: Not counted (fetch of the home page timed out). One 2023 note says Musk's tweets were searchable on mobile via from:elonmusk at that time (unverified).
ui_notes: Note page with the note text and the linked post ID; date shown on the note.
note: Notes are user-written, so they are pointers, not verdicts. Post embeds are no longer reliable.

name: Zenodo: Auditing Elon Musk's Impact on Hate Speech and Bots (datasets)
what: Research dataset of tweet IDs and daily counts around Musk's Oct-Nov 2022 ownership period, plus hate-word tweets.
why_it_matters: A citable Musk-tweet dataset with IDs and dates. Can be used to recover text for IDs we hold, and to check our 92k Zenodo CSVs for gaps in 2022.
numbers: Data 197.5 MB total. Tweet-ID files cover 2022; hate-level file covers 2022-10-01 to 2022-11-30. Record count not stated on page. Views 170, downloads 22 at fetch.
ui_notes: Data only: CSV tweet IDs with dates; frequency CSVs; Perspective API attribute columns on hate-word tweets (names not listed).
note: Text and engagement not included in ID files. Files restricted and require login to check access (per fetch). CC BY 4.0.

name: Hugging Face: MasaFoundation/elonmusk_elon_tweets
what: Small Elon Musk tweet dataset in Parquet.
why_it_matters: Free and easy to load, but tiny. Useful as a cross-check against our 92k set only.
numbers: 1K to 10K rows (dataset card size category, per search snippet). Exact count not verified.
ui_notes: Hugging Face dataset viewer (table of rows).
note: Not fetched; URL taken from search result (commit page). Provenance and license unknown.

name: Kaggle: Elon Musk tweets Jan-Oct 2022 (via secondary analysis)
what: Kaggle-hosted Musk tweet CSVs (2021 tweets paired with Dogecoin prices; a 2022 set covering 27 Jan to 27 Oct 2022).
why_it_matters: Public, free Musk tweet CSVs with timestamp and tweet ID. Good for overlap checks with our Zenodo set.
numbers: 2022 set covers 27 Jan to 27 Oct 2022 at about 11 tweets per day (per a secondary analysis). Row counts not verified.
ui_notes: Kaggle dataset page: file preview table.
note: Kaggle itself returned only a title on fetch; the URL is a third-party mirror. Coverage gaps likely.

name: Gumroad: elon tweets (paid CSV)
what: Paid CSV of Musk tweets with ID, text, date and engagement counts.
why_it_matters: Only off-the-shelf Musk set with engagement fields we found; claims more than 20,000 tweets. Compare with our 92k before paying.
numbers: Claims 20,000+ tweets (listing); search summary says 20200+ rows at $0.99. Collection method not stated.
ui_notes: Product listing page; file preview not available to us.
note: Not fetched; provenance unknown. Treat as unverified. | check: lowbyte.gumroad.com listing shows '20200+ elon musk tweets' (matches); the $0.99 price was not visible in the fetched page.

name: Filmot (YouTube subtitle search)
what: Search engine over YouTube subtitles, titles and metadata, with channel filters and boolean operators.
why_it_matters: The main free way to find what a named YouTuber or channel said across transcripts. Covers the YouTube half of 'everything said'.
numbers: Page states over 1.7 billion caption tracks across 1.5 billion videos and 84 million channels; metadata index over 18 billion videos (page in Vietnamese, translated by us).
ui_notes: Search box; channel picker (include/exclude, up to 200 channels per search); title filter; subtitle type (auto vs manual); operators: quoted phrase, |, NEAR/N, NOTNEAR/N, -word. Timestamp deep links and API not confirmed on the page.
note: Filmot's Python package wraps an API that needs a RapidAPI account (per PyPI listing). Deep-link timestamps not confirmed. | check: filmot.com (Vietnamese UI): over 1.7 billion (Tỷ) caption/transcript records across 1.5B videos and 84M channels; 18B metadata videos; matches row.

name: YouGlish
what: Pronunciation search over YouTube clips for a word or phrase.
why_it_matters: Not a person archive. Listed only to rule it out for 'what did X say'.
numbers: 25 language options; English accent filters (US, UK, AU, CA, IE, SCO, NZ). No coverage count on page.
ui_notes: Phrase search returning short video clips; context tags such as #Obama appear.
note: Out of scope for person archives; included to close the question.

name: Listen Notes podcast search and API
what: Podcast search engine with an API; transcripts available as an option on episode lookup.
why_it_matters: Lets us search podcast episodes for a person's name and pull episode metadata at scale. Transcript coverage is the limit.
numbers: About 3.3M podcasts and 190M+ episodes; free tier 300 requests/month; commercial around $200/month (GTM Directory, secondary, approximate).
ui_notes: API docs; search returns episodes with publish date and podcast name; transcript via episode endpoint option (per tutorial).
note: Figures from a third-party directory, not Listen Notes itself. Confirm pricing on their pricing page. | check: listennotes.com API pricing (en): free tier is 150 requests/month, not 300; $200/month base fee for 1+ requests matches the row's commercial figure.

name: Taddy podcast API (and Podcast Index comparison)
what: Podcast API vendor whose blog says Podcast Index has no episode search and transcripts exist for under 1% of its episodes.
why_it_matters: Sets the realistic ceiling on free podcast transcripts: most open feeds have no transcript. Transcripts are a paid feature on Taddy.
numbers: Podcast Index transcripts for under 1% of episodes (competitor claim). Taddy developers page: transcripts and webhooks are paid.
ui_notes: API; episode objects; transcript endpoint (paid).
note: Competitor marketing source; verify against Podcast Index docs before use.

name: Tapesearch (podcast transcript search)
what: Podcast transcript search: exact-phrase and keyword search across episodes, with date filters, alerts and an API.
why_it_matters: Closest to a per-speaker 'every podcast they said X on' search we found. Gives episode-level timestamps, which matters for quote dating.
numbers: Two conflicting counts: over 878,000 transcripts (one source) and 330,739 AI transcripts from 2,298 podcasts (older source). Pricing tiers: Basic, Pro, Alerts.
ui_notes: Search titles, summaries and transcripts; sort by relevance or podcast; filter by start/end date, last 6 or 12 months; exact phrase with quotes; exclude words; export TXT, SRT, VTT, JSON; AI Q&A across podcasts.
note: URL is a third-party tool listing; official site not fetched. Transcript errors on names noted by a review.

name: Snipd (podcast player with transcript search and quote clips)
what: Podcast app with per-episode transcripts, in-transcript search, saved snippets and shareable quote cards.
why_it_matters: Shows a quote-capture UI (speaker-labelled transcript, timestamped clip, AI summary). Pattern for our quote card, not an archive.
numbers: No archive count found.
ui_notes: Search within transcripts; snippet with transcript and AI summary; quote cards for sharing; headphone-tap capture (third-party review).
note: Podscribe search returned nothing; not covered.

name: Huberman Lab official transcripts (Premium) and PodcastRex
what: Official episode transcripts behind a paid tier, searchable by topic, guest and keyword in the dashboard; third-party PodcastRex transcripts with speaker labels.
why_it_matters: A creator-run transcript index with search, so it is a model for a single-person archive. Shows the paid-gate reality for a person's own archive.
numbers: PodcastRex lists 30 of 794 Huberman episodes transcribed (free preview).
ui_notes: Official dashboard lists transcripts by episode type and date, with a search bar (topic, guest, keyword); transcript tab on each episode page. PodcastRex: speaker-labelled transcript per episode.
note: Huberman is not a person in our slice; included as the best single-creator transcript index pattern.

name: Lex Fridman transcript sources (transcript.lol; Lexicap)
what: Third-party Whisper-style transcripts of Lex Fridman episodes; transcript.lol lists user-requested episodes only.
why_it_matters: Lex Fridman's long-form interviews include many Musk appearances; a per-episode transcript is the raw input for dated quotes.
numbers: transcript.lol: 13 items (per search summary). Lexicap: described as Whisper transcripts for all episodes, but the karpathy.ai page we fetched did not describe the project.
ui_notes: transcript.lol: per-episode transcript page, request-a-transcript form. Lexicap: zip of raw captions (per search summary).
note: Lexicap URL did not confirm on fetch (returned Karpathy homepage). Treat Lexicap as unverified.

name: Paul Graham essay index (paulgraham.com)
what: Complete list of Paul Graham essays on one page.
why_it_matters: A clean full-corpus list for a single author, but undated on the index. Shows that even good archives often lack a date at the list level.
numbers: About 235 entries, about 233 essays plus 2 book chapters (manual count). Only explicit year on the page: 1998 (Viaweb snapshot).
ui_notes: Plain title list; each link goes to an essay that carries its own date line.
note: Essays are the author's own writing, not spoken quotes; included as a 'complete corpus' benchmark. | check: paulgraham.com/articles.html: 246 unique .html links, which includes a few non-essay pages; row says about 235 entries (within 10%).

name: Quotewise (Naval Ravikant tweet-style quotes)
what: Quote aggregator with one page per line, each carrying a source attribution; premium advanced filters by source and date.
why_it_matters: Only per-person quote archive we found for Naval; no official nav.al search. Shows the risk: a quote-check of seven popular Naval lines found 6 with no original located and 1 with no reliable source.
numbers: Not counted. Secondary check: 6 of 7 popular lines consistently credited but original not located; 1 with no reliable source.
ui_notes: One page per quote with source line; premium search filters by source, date and more.
note: Borderline generic quote site; kept only for the per-person source pattern. Fact-check source for the 6-of-7 claim not fetched.
